title: Hom of complexes and total tensor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet$ be cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then there is an isomorphism of complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules

$$
 \mathcal Hom^\bullet\bigl(\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)\bigr)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal L^\bullet),\mathcal M^\bullet\bigr),
$$

with the Hom complexes of [def-pur-hom-complex] and the total tensor complex of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], functorial in $\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet$.

source.place: Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-compose (Tag 0A90); for ringed spaces cohomology-lemma-compose (Tag 0A8M)

proof.text: For each integer n, expand the degree-n term of the left Hom complex using [def-pur-hom-complex]: it is the product over p and q of sheaf-linear maps from K^p tensor L^q to M^{p+q+n}. The degree-n term on the right is the product over r of maps from the direct sum over p+q=r of K^p tensor L^q to M^{r+n}; by the universal property of the direct sum this is the same product over p,q. The identifications use the total-tensor definition [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the tensor-Hom adjunction for sheaves of O-modules on a site [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], applied over each object U of C to the restricted modules on the localized site C/U (a site with the sheaf of rings O|_U), so that the sheaf-Hom terms are identified sectionwise compatibly with restriction.

Under the degreewise identification, a homogeneous family f=(f_{p,q}) on the left is sent to the unique map on each total-degree summand whose restriction to K^p tensor L^q is the currying of f_{p,q}; explicitly, it sends x tensor y to f_{p,q}(x)(y). Conversely, restrict a map from the total tensor to every summand K^p tensor L^q and uncurry it. The module tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] gives existence and uniqueness on every summand, so these constructions are mutually inverse degreewise.

source.place: Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-compose (Tag 0A90), proof of the Hom-total-tensor correspondence

proof.text: The correspondence is a chain map. For a component of bidegree (p,q), the Hom differential is d_M f - (-1)^n f d_K on the outer Hom and, inside the inner Hom, d_M g - (-1)^{p+n} g d_L. The total-tensor differential on K^p tensor L^q is d_K tensor 1 + (-1)^p 1 tensor d_L [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Applying the two sides to x tensor y gives the same four terms, with the L-differential term acquiring the factor (-1)^p and the Hom-degree sign producing exactly the factor (-1)^n; hence the displayed correspondence commutes with differentials. This is the direct Koszul-sign verification from the Hom-complex formula [def-pur-hom-complex].

The inverse constructions commute with maps of K, L, and M because they are defined componentwise by composition and the tensor-Hom adjunction is natural. Therefore the chain isomorphism is functorial in all three complexes.
